startup.name: TraceRoot.AI
startup.one_liner: The open-source platform that continuously improves your ai agents
startup.description: Open source observability platform for AI agents that finds patterns in production issues and hands verified fixes to a coding agent. Engineering teams building agents pay for the hosted product; a team of 4 in San Francisco, YC Summer 2025.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting rate of about 1 percent for a random applicant from references/yc_acceptance.md. Up for a technical team in a topical category (AI agent infrastructure, open source) and a clear developer problem; down for a crowded space with funded open source rivals and a team of 4 with no stated revenue. The company is already listed in Summer 2025, so the ladder is the "if accepted" view.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say the space is crowded: several YC alumni already ship open source LLM tracing and evaluation, so the pitch needs unusual evidence of usage or a sharper wedge than another tracing dashboard, and a four person team with no stated revenue gives them little proof to weigh against that.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --tag "Developer Tools" --calibration-only: seed 55% known only, 59% upper (n=29); B2B 2022-2025 seed 59% known only, 65% upper (n=126). Time to seed p75 about 15 months from batch start.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 16 months from 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17 (the Summer 2025 batch start). About three quarters of eventual seeds land inside 16 months, so the ever anchor of 0.55 to 0.59 scales to about 0.43, then I move up by under 1.25 times because open source agent tooling drew many seeds in 2025. This number does not rank the company against others in the batch.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M from angels, a seed fund or a strategic. Most common when the product has early users but no paid base.
Institutional seed in the middle of the 2022 and later table, led by a seed fund after a few months of visible traction.
Larger institutional seed, usually needing paying customers or a standout team story and a competitive process.
Upside seed from a top tier fund in a hot category; rare and needs clear momentum.

ladder.why_it_fails: The most likely miss is that the category is already crowded with funded open source rivals (Langfuse, Traceloop, Helicone, Laminar, Confident AI) and a four person team with no stated paying customers cannot show growth beyond GitHub stars. Investors in 2025 funded LLM observability at seed, but the well known rounds of this kind went to teams with early enterprise users, so a stars only story ends in the YC deal plus angels under $1M.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only: series A 15% known only, 29% upper, cond 26% (n=74)
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window effect: only 3 to 9 months can remain between a seed and 2026-11-17, and time to Series A from batch start has a median near 29 months in 2022 and later batches. The ever conditional of 0.26 scaled for that window is about 0.08.

bands.rationale: Thin Series A or extended seed style round after slow revenue; sized like the lower quartile of 2022 and later rounds.
Core Series A near the 2022 and later median of $14M with a pre money in the market range of $50M to $65M.
Strong round after fast growth and a competitive process.
Hot category outlier round, similar to the largest AI Series A rounds.

ladder.why_it_fails: Observability for agents is a tooling category where buyers can swap vendors cheaply and cloud and database vendors bundle the same features. Reaching Series A needs seven figure annual revenue from teams that have budgets, and the analogs (Baserun, Helicone) stalled or sold early without a Series A when LangSmith and Langfuse took mindshare.

anchors.source: same command: series B 2% known only, 18% upper, cond 16% (n=19)
anchors.adjustment_reason: Series B inside the window requires two more rounds in under 16 months, which almost no company in the data did; the 0.16 conditional is cut by about two thirds.

bands.rationale: Flat or modest Series B because growth slowed.
Typical Series B near the 2022 and later median of $37M.
Upside Series B after strong growth, priced near the top of the 2022 and later table.

ladder.why_it_fails: Reaching Series B in this window would need very fast revenue growth and a position as a category leader; the category is consolidating through acquisitions, which is a more common end than a large independent round, so investors at this stage would likely pass on a growth round and the team would need to sell or stay small.

anchors.source: same command: series C 0% known only, 16% upper, cond 0% (n=3), too thin; used the all era calibration conditional of 36 percent (n=55) from references/stage_benchmarks.md and widened
anchors.adjustment_reason: Three further rounds in 16 months is extreme; p reflects the window, not the ever conditional.

bands.rationale: Modest Series C near the 2022 and later median of $45M.
Typical growth round for a company with clear category leadership and rising revenue.
Late stage upside round for a category leader, rare in the sample (n=9 since 2022).

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C or later inside the window would require a breakout like the largest AI infrastructure companies; for a four person team in an acquisition prone category this is very unlikely, and no analog in the data that was this young reached it in the same span.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most paths end in stalling or a small acquisition. Open source observability tools are often bought by database or cloud vendors for their users and engineers, as Langfuse and Traceloop style outcomes suggest, and a four person team rarely gets to a billion dollar exit before a larger player copies the features.

analogs.relevance: Open source LLM observability from Winter 2023.
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a $4M seed in November 2023, about 10 months after batch, with a popular open source repo.

analogs.relevance: Open source tracing standard plus commercial platform.
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a $6.1M seed in May 2025, more than two years after its Winter 2023 batch, so seeds can come late.

analogs.relevance: Open source evals project turned company, Winter 2025.
analogs.outcome_summary: Closed a $2.2M seed in March 2025 on GitHub adoption, a small round.

analogs.relevance: LLM observability and testing, Summer 2023, two person team.
analogs.outcome_summary: No round found; the category filled with Langfuse, LangSmith and Helicone.
Stayed small and was later listed acquired.

killers.risk: Category crowding and commoditization of tracing
killers.evidence: Langfuse, Traceloop, Helicone, Baserun and Confident AI all launched open source tracing and evaluation from YC alone.
killers.mitigation: Pick one wedge, the verified fix loop with coding agents, and show measured fix acceptance rates.

killers.risk: Platform bundling by cloud, database and model vendors
killers.evidence: Observability is a natural feature of database, cloud and model providers; Langfuse took a ClickHouse backed path and Datadog sells LLM monitoring.
killers.mitigation: Stay vendor neutral and open source so teams trust the data layer.

killers.risk: Open source does not convert to paying customers
killers.evidence: Confident AI and similar projects had GitHub traction but only a small $2.2M seed.
killers.mitigation: Ship the hosted team features early and sell to the first 10 design partners.

killers.risk: Four person team cannot cover enterprise needs such as security reviews and on premise support
killers.evidence: Enterprise buyers of observability ask for SOC 2 and single sign on, which absorb engineering time.
killers.mitigation: Delay enterprise until product led revenue pays for it.

technical_complexity.rationale: Collecting traces is easy; clustering production failures, producing a verified fix and testing it against a coding agent is hard, but a small team of strong engineers can build a first version in three months. Model and agent frameworks change quickly, so maintenance is the cost.

takeover_risk.rationale: Any observability vendor can add agent trace views in a few quarters, and framework owners already ship their own tracing, so the feature can be absorbed. The open source license gives the startup some trust but does not stop bundling.

evidence.claim: Agent and LLM observability has many funded vendors and roundups listing a dozen platforms, which shows paid demand from teams shipping agents.

roadmap.goal: Show real usage by teams running agents in production.
actions: Publish the open source repo with a one command setup and collect issues from real users
Land 5 design partners who run agents in production and record their fix rates
roadmap.proof: Weekly active self hosted deployments and 5 named design partners

roadmap.goal: Convert open source usage into paid revenue before the 16 month window ends.
actions: Launch a hosted tier with team features and usage pricing
Publish a benchmark showing fixes verified per week versus manual debugging
roadmap.proof: $20K or more monthly recurring revenue from at least 10 paying teams

roadmap.goal: Be the default loop between observability and coding agents.
actions: Integrate with the main coding agents so fixes open as pull requests
Hire a first enterprise account executive and finish SOC 2
roadmap.proof: Seven figure annual recurring revenue with net revenue retention above 120 percent

pros.point: Open source distribution gives a low cost path to developer adoption
pros.evidence: Langfuse and Confident AI both converted open source use into seed rounds.

pros.point: Timing: agents entering production create a debugging need
pros.evidence: Market roundups list a dozen funded observability vendors for agents, so budgets exist.

brand.name: TraceRoot.AI
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "TraceRoot.AI" --era 2022+: 9 characters, 2 words, compound words kind.
strengths: Describes the tracing and root cause job
weaknesses: Dot AI suffix is common and generic
brand.rationale: The name says what the product does, like Langfuse or Traceloop, but the AI suffix and similarity to Traceloop limit memorability. Descriptive developer tool names rarely hurt and do not drive growth.

narrative.headline: A fair seed candidate in a crowded open source category where the next step depends on paying teams, not stars.
narrative.general_summary: TraceRoot.AI is an open source observability product for AI agents that aims to turn production failures into verified fixes. The category was already full in mid 2025, with Langfuse, Traceloop, Helicone and LangSmith all funded and Braintrust leading in evals. Comparable YC companies show that seed rounds of about $2M to $6M were available to teams with open source adoption, but several others stayed small. For a 16 month window the seed probability is close to the windowed cohort anchor, and later rounds are unlikely inside it. The odds do not rank this company above other batch companies.

assumptions: Blind forecast from the YC listing only: no revenue, user or investor data was available.
Window is 16.3 months, 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17. Seed means an outside round above about $1M closing in that window.
Cohort anchors are for reaching a round ever and were scaled down by about one quarter for the window.
